description: Car Hacking Village at DEF CON 30 focuses on automotive cybersecurity, CAN bus reverse engineering, connected car telematics exploitation, ECU fuzzing, and vehicle biometrics.

talks.title: Security Like the 80s: How I Stole Your RF
talks.teaser: Ayyapan Rajesh details CVE-2022-27254, demonstrating how unencrypted fixed rolling codes in Honda remote keyless entry systems allow replay and vehicle theft.
talks.summary:
The Illusion of Security in Modern Wireless Keys

While remote keyless entry (RKE) systems offer immense convenience, many automotive manufacturers continue to deploy insecure wireless protocols lacking cryptographic integrity.

Discovering Fixed Rolling Codes (CVE-2022-27254)

Ayyapan Rajesh explains the discovery of a critical vulnerability in Honda RKE implementations where radio frequency counter synchronization is absent or non-enforced.

Executing Replay and Vehicle Takeover Attacks

The author demonstrates capturing sub-GHz key fob RF transmissions over the air and replaying the unencrypted signal to unlock doors, pop trunks, and start vehicle engines.

Cryptographic Modernization for Automotive RF

The presentation calls for universal adoption of challenge-response mutual authentication and secure rolling code algorithms across consumer vehicles.

talks.title: Smart Black Box Fuzzing for Real-World Automotive ECUs
talks.teaser: Researchers present smart black-box fuzzing for automotive ECUs, generating protocol-aware UDS CAN testcases and handling recovery without coverage feedback.
talks.summary:
The Challenges of Black-Box Vehicle Fuzzing

Performing security fuzzing on production automotive ECUs is hindered by the inability to instrument binary coverage and the unpredictability of hardware crash states.

Generating Protocol-Aware UDS CAN Testcases

Soohwan Oh, Jonghyuk Song, and Jeongho Yang design testcase generators informed by Unified Diagnostic Services (UDS) message flows, service IDs, and frame formatting.

Detecting Sub-System Errors and Negative Response Codes

The speakers outline automated heuristics to detect silent ECU failures by tracking timeouts, Negative Response Codes (NRCs), and Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs).

Automating Recovery and Continuous Testing

The authors demonstrate automated session reset procedures using `ClearDiagnosticInformation` and `ECUReset` commands to keep target ECUs alive during extended fuzzing runs.

talks.title: RFCommotion: Invisible Serial Ports Flying Through the Air
talks.teaser: Kamel introduces RFCommotion, an open-source auditing tool for testing Bluetooth RFCOMM virtual serial port services attached to vehicle head units and IoT devices.
talks.summary:
The Complex Protocol Stack of Modern Bluetooth

Bluetooth encompasses multiple sub-protocols layered together, with Radio Frequency Communication (RFCOMM) emulating RS-232 serial ports over wireless links.

Auditing In-Vehicle RFCOMM Channels

Kamel explores how automotive infotainment head units and telematics modules expose unauthenticated or poorly segmented RFCOMM endpoints.

Introducing the RFCommotion Testing Framework

The author demonstrates RFCommotion, an open-source tool developed to enumerate, fuzz, and interact with RFCOMM serial channels attached to automotive microcontrollers.

Hardening In-Vehicle Bluetooth Stacks

The presentation provides recommendations for automotive software architects on implementing strict pairing policies, service authorization, and channel segregation.

talks.title: Remote Exploitation of Honda Connected Vehicles via Telematics APIs
talks.teaser: Mohammed Shine uncovers broken access controls in Honda Connect APIs, allowing unauthorized attackers to remotely unlock doors, start engines, and honk horns.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Attack Surface of Mobile Connected Car Apps

Modern vehicles increasingly integrate companion mobile applications that communicate with cloud backend servers to execute remote vehicle management commands.

Auditing Honda Connect API Endpoints

Mohammed Shine analyzes the REST APIs powering the Honda Connect mobile application for 5th generation Honda City vehicles, identifying broken object-level access controls.

Executing Remote Actions via Telematics Control Units (TCUs)

The author demonstrates manipulating API requests to send unauthorized commands directly to target vehicle TCUs—including locking/unlocking doors and remote engine starts.

Securing Connected Vehicle Cloud Backends

The presentation outlines crucial API security controls, token authorization checks, and mutual TLS validation required for automotive telematics backends.

talks.title: Integrating Mileage Clocking into an Immersive Vehicle Hacking Simulator
talks.teaser: David Rogers integrates commercial mileage clocking tools and remote braking overrides into an immersive vehicle simulator rig to safely study cyber-physical attacks.
talks.summary:
The Threat of Illicit Mileage Clocking Tools

Commercial 'mileage correction' hardware tools are widely available on the gray market, allowing bad actors to manipulate digital odometer clusters and vehicle logs.

Constructing a Vehicle Hacking Simulation Rig

David Rogers details building a full-scale automotive simulator incorporating instrument clusters, head units, dashcams, and CAN bus testbenches.

Simulating Dangerous Remote Overrides and Brake Failures

Rogers demonstrates adapting the simulator to demonstrate terrifying cyber-physical scenarios—such as remotely disabling accelerator and brake response in a moving vehicle.

Standardizing Security for Autonomous and Connected Fleets

The author discusses regulatory frameworks, hardware security modules (HSMs), and cryptographic log integrity needed to protect modern connected vehicles.

talks.title: Getting Naughty on CAN Bus with the CHV Badge
talks.teaser: Evadsnibor shows how the DEF CON 30 Car Hacking Village badge uses the Raspberry Pi RP2040 microcontroller to generate interactive CAN waveforms and disrupt vehicle buses.
talks.summary:
The Hardware Architecture of the DC30 CHV Badge

The DEF CON 30 Car Hacking Village badge is powered by the dual-core ARM Cortex-M0+ Raspberry Pi RP2040 microcontroller paired with dedicated CAN transceivers.

Generating Arbitrary CAN Waveforms with Programmable I/O (PIO)

Evadsnibor demonstrates leveraging the RP2040's unique PIO state machines to synthesize raw physical-layer digital waveforms and inject bus-level bit errors.

Interactive Waveform Manipulation and Network Disruption

The author illustrates how the badge reacts dynamically to network traffic, mutating waveforms in real time based on ECU response frames to disrupt communications.

Unlocking Low-Cost Automotive Hardware Tooling

The presentation highlights the potential of affordable, open-source microcontrollers for advanced automotive physical-layer security research.

talks.title: canTot: A Modular CLI Framework for CAN Bus Hacking & Pentesting
talks.teaser: Jay Turla introduces canTot, a modular command-line framework that consolidates automotive exploits, fuzzers, and CAN bus vulnerability modules in Python.
talks.summary:
The Need for Unified Automotive Penetration Testing Tools

While penetration testers have established frameworks like Metasploit and Recon-ng, automotive security tools have historically remained fragmented across disjointed scripts.

Introducing the canTot CLI Architecture

Jay Turla presents canTot, an open-source modular framework designed to simplify vehicle penetration testing and Python-based CAN bus development.

Consolidating Known Automotive Exploits and Fuzzers

Turla walks through canTot modules—including CAN frame sniffers, ECU identifier scanners, known CVE exploit modules, and payload injection utilities.

Streamlining Automotive Security Auditing Workflows

The author demonstrates how researchers and hobbyists can easily script custom modules to evaluate connected vehicle ECUs and diagnostic gateways.

talks.title: CANalyse 2.0: Automated Vehicle Network Analysis & Injection Platform
talks.teaser: Kartheek Lade presents CANalyse 2.0, a vehicle network analysis tool featuring automated dataset filtration, SQL-based log querying, and Telegram bot injection.
talks.summary:
Managing the Complexity of High-Speed CAN Logs

Vehicle networks generate millions of CAN frames every minute, making manual log triage and anomaly isolation overwhelming for security analysts.

Three Operational Modes of CANalyse 2.0

Kartheek Lade introduces CANalyse 2.0, detailing Smart Scan for automated unique packet filtering, an integrated IDE powered by pandasql, and Telegram bot integration.

Rapid Packet Querying and Payload Injection

Lade demonstrates querying vehicle packet databases using standard SQL syntax and injecting crafted CAN payloads back into the target vehicle in real time.

Remote Automotive Testing via Telegram

The author showcases triggering CAN diagnostic requests and monitoring ECU responses remotely using smartphone Telegram chat commands.

talks.title: Biometrics System Hacking in Modern Smart Vehicles
talks.teaser: Kevin2600 and Li Swei demonstrate bypassing in-vehicle facial recognition and voiceprint biometric systems to authenticate, start engines, and execute hidden commands.
talks.summary:
The Rise of In-Vehicle Biometric Authentication

Automakers increasingly integrate facial recognition cameras and voiceprint microphones into vehicle cabins for driver profiles, keyless ignition, and in-car shopping.

Attacking In-Cabin Facial Recognition Systems

Kevin2600 and Li Swei demonstrate practical presentation attacks using printed photos, digital screens, and 3D silicone masks to bypass driver authentication and start engines.

Spoofing Voiceprint Systems with Acoustic Audio Injection

The researchers show how to synthesize victim voiceprints and embed ultrasonic or psychoacoustically hidden voice commands inside music tracks (e.g., 'Open the car window').

Securing Multi-Modal Biometrics in Automotive Design

The authors recommend liveness detection algorithms, IR depth sensing, and multi-factor physical confirmation for critical automotive controls.
